background.executionContext:
**Commands used (chronologically):**
1. `pwsh ./b4w.ps1 help` — load help output (direct `./b4w.ps1` failed due to CRLF shebang; used `pwsh` explicitly)
2. `pwsh ./b4w.ps1 crawl --help` — inspect crawl subcommand flags
3. `pwsh ./b4w.ps1 goto "http://books.toscrape.com/"` — navigate to site, inspect page structure
4. `pwsh ./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot capture` — capture HTML snapshot for inspection
5. `pwsh ./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot get all attr 'a[href]' href --limit 50` — extract link hrefs to understand URL patterns
6. `pwsh ./b4w.ps1 crawl ... -ol 'a[href*="catalogue"]' -olp '.*catalogue.*' -tl 10 -d 1 --format table` — first crawl attempt (link discovery — **failed: 0 pages**)
7. Multiple retries with simpler selectors (`a[href]`, `a`) — all **failed: 0 pages**
8. Switch to `https://` — got 1 page but no out-links
9. Inspected `crawl result` JSON → discovered root cause: `"No qualifying bean of type 'ai.platon.pulsar.loop.TaskLoops' available"`
10. Created seed file with 3 book detail URLs → `pwsh ./b4w.ps1 crawl --seed-file ... --depth 0 --format table` — **3 pages found**
11. `pwsh ./b4w.ps1 crawl --seed-file ... --depth 0 --format csv -o results.csv` — CSV **written but plain text** (no `--sql`)
12. Created X-SQL query file (`extract.sql`) → re-ran with `--sql @file --format json` — **valid JSON with extracted fields**
13. `pwsh ./b4w.ps1 crawl --seed-file ... --sql @file --format table` — **proper table output**
14. `pwsh ./b4w.ps1 crawl --seed-file ... --sql @file --format csv --output file.csv` — **proper CSV written**
15. `pwsh ./b4w.ps1 crawl list` — **21 tracked tasks shown**
16. `pwsh ./b4w.ps1 crawl clear` — **29 backend tasks cleared**

**Workarounds required:**
- Used `pwsh ./b4w.ps1` instead of `./b4w.sh` or `./b4w.ps1` because CRLF line endings break the shebang
- Used `--seed-file` + `--depth 0` (bulk fetch) instead of link discovery because crawl link extraction is broken
- Used `--sql @file` for X-SQL extraction because inline SQL quoting is fragile
- Created `.test-sessions/` directory manually for all outputs
background.task:
The task was **partially successful**. Here's what worked and what didn't:

| Step | Description | Outcome |
|------|-------------|---------|
| 1 | Crawl with depth 1, link selector, link pattern, top-links 10, table format | ❌ **Blocked** — link discovery fails with backend `TaskLoops` bean error |
| 2 | Re-run as CSV with `--output` | ⚠️ **Partial** — works with `--sql` + `--depth 0` seed-file mode, not link discovery |
| 3 | Re-run as JSON | ⚠️ **Partial** — same limitation; JSON output is correct when X-SQL is used |
| 4 | Seed file with 2–3 book detail URLs, crawl with `--seed-file` | ✅ **Works** (seed-file bulk-fetch mode, depth 0) |
| 5 | List crawl history with `crawl list` | ✅ **Works** — shows 21 tracked tasks with timestamps and status |

**Data extracted successfully via X-SQL:**
```
price   | title                | url
--------+----------------------+-------------------------------------------------------
£51.77  | A Light in the Attic | https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/a-light-in-the-attic_1000/index.html
```

**Key blocker:** Crawl link discovery (`depth >= 1`) is completely broken due to a missing Spring bean (`ai.platon.pulsar.loop.TaskLoops`). All CSS selectors (even bare `a`) return zero matches. The bulk-fetch mode (`--depth 0` + `--seed-file`) works but suffers from an intermittent "protocol handler not ready" error on pages beyond the first, and ~100s startup delays on every crawl invocation.

issues.title: Crawl link discovery completely broken — missing TaskLoops Spring bean

sections.body: pwsh ./b4w.ps1 crawl 'https://books.toscrape.com/' -ol 'a' -d 1 -tl 3 --refresh
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The crawl extracts links matching the CSS selector and follows them up to the specified depth.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Crawl completes with 0 out-links found. The crawl result JSON reveals: 'No qualifying bean of type ai.platon.pulsar.loop.TaskLoops available'. Every CSS selector including bare 'a' returns zero matches. The portal page itself loads (page found at depth 0), but link discovery never executes.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The crawl's link-discovery pipeline requires a Spring bean 'ai.platon.pulsar.loop.TaskLoops' that is not registered in the application context when running from the locally-built JAR. This could be a missing component scan, a conditional bean that evaluates to false in dev mode, or a missing module dependency.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-rest or browser4-core — the Spring configuration that should register TaskLoops bean
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Ensure TaskLoops is registered as a Spring bean (check @ComponentScan base packages, @Conditional annotations)
- Add a fallback or null-safe path in the crawl link extractor so link discovery degrades gracefully rather than silently returning 0 results
- Add a clear error message to the CLI output when this bean is missing, rather than showing 'matched zero elements'
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: No way to complete the task as documented — crawl link discovery fundamentally broken

sections.body: Any crawl command with depth >= 1: pwsh ./b4w.ps1 crawl <url> -ol <any-selector> -d 1
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Links are discovered from the portal page and followed to depth 1.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Link discovery always returns 0 results regardless of CSS selector, URL, or flags. The documented core crawl workflow (navigate portal → extract links → follow to detail pages) is completely non-functional.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Combination of the TaskLoops bean missing (Issue 2) and the protocol handler issue (Issue 3). Even if link discovery worked, the handler would likely fail on subsequent pages.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Fix the TaskLoops bean registration (Issue 2) and protocol handler lifecycle (Issue 3)
- After fixes, run the documented crawl workflow end-to-end as a validation test
- Add an integration test that verifies link discovery on a known test site like books.toscrape.com
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: CRLF line endings in b4w.ps1 break direct execution on Linux

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 help
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The script executes via the pwsh shebang.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: /usr/bin/env: 'pwsh\r': No such file or directory
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The b4w.ps1 file uses Windows CRLF line terminators. The shebang line ends with \r, which /usr/bin/env treats as part of the executable name. pwsh 7.6.3 IS installed at /opt/microsoft/powershell/7/pwsh, but the CR causes the lookup to fail.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: b4w.ps1:1 — shebang line
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Convert b4w.ps1 line endings to LF (Unix) using dos2unix or a git attribute (.gitattributes: b4w.ps1 text eol=lf)
- Alternative: add a b4w.sh wrapper that invokes pwsh -File b4w.ps1, which already exists but should be the documented primary entry point on Linux
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Crawl bulk fetch fails for pages beyond the first — 'protocol handler not ready'

sections.body:
pwsh ./b4w.ps1 crawl --seed-file .test-sessions/book-seeds.txt --depth 0 --sql @.test-sessions/extract.sql --format json
(seed file contains 3 distinct book URLs)
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: All 3 pages load and X-SQL extraction produces 3 rows of results.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Only the first page loads successfully (contentLength: 12787, extracted fields correct). Pages 2 and 3 fail with contentLength: 0 and extractionError: 'fetch returned 0 bytes (possible protocol handler not ready)'. This pattern is 100% reproducible across multiple crawl invocations.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The HTTP protocol handler (likely OkHttp or similar) used for page fetching appears to close, crash, or become unregistered after the first successful request, causing subsequent fetches to return 0 bytes. The error message suggests the handler is not 'ready' rather than timing out or returning an HTTP error.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-core — the page fetch/protocol handler initialization and lifecycle management
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Investigate the protocol handler lifecycle — ensure it is properly re-initialized or reused between page fetches within a single crawl session
- Add a retry mechanism for the 'protocol handler not ready' error (at least 3 retries with backoff)
- Consider whether the handler needs per-request instantiation rather than a shared instance
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: htmlsnapshot query (X-SQL) returns 417 'Expectation Failed' while crawl --sql works on same page

sections.body:
pwsh ./b4w.ps1 htmlsnapshot query --sql @extract.sql 'https://books.toscrape.com/catalogue/a-light-in-the-attic_1000/index.html'
(using the same SQL file that works with crawl --sql)
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: X-SQL extraction returns results identical to crawl --sql on the same page.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Returns status 417 'Expectation Failed' with empty resultSet, even though pageStatusCode: 200 and pageContentBytes: 12787 confirm the page loaded successfully. The same SQL file and same URL work perfectly through crawl --seed-file --depth 0 --sql.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The htmlsnapshot query code path uses a different X-SQL execution pipeline than crawl --sql. The 417 status suggests the X-SQL query engine or template processor fails validation in the htmlsnapshot pathway while succeeding in the crawl pathway. The @url placeholder resolution might differ between the two paths.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-rest — MCPToolController or X-SQL query executor for htmlsnapshot vs crawl paths
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Unify the X-SQL execution pipeline between htmlsnapshot query and crawl --sql
- Add detailed error information to the 417 response (current response only has empty resultSet)
- Document the known difference or fix so both paths produce consistent results
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Crawl startup delays — consistently 96+ seconds before processing begins

sections.body: pwsh ./b4w.ps1 crawl --seed-file .test-sessions/book-seeds.txt --depth 0 --format table
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Crawl processing begins within a few seconds of submission.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Every crawl invocation shows 'Still waiting for crawl to start...' messages at 16-second intervals, taking 80-96 seconds before processing begins. This happens even after running 'crawl clear' to remove terminal tasks, and regardless of whether 1 or 3 URLs are submitted.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The crawl backend appears to have a fixed polling interval (16s) and the queue/worker startup takes multiple cycles. This could be due to worker thread pool exhaustion, a stuck previous task holding a lock, or the scheduler using a pessimistic polling strategy.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-rest — crawl task scheduler or worker pool configuration
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Reduce the polling interval from 16s to 2-3s for the first few checks
- Ensure completed tasks release worker threads immediately
- Add a --nowait flag for immediate synchronous submission to the worker pool
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: X-SQL function naming inconsistent between crawl reference and X-SQL reference docs

sections.body: Compare skills/browser4-cli/references/crawl.md examples vs skills/browser4-cli/references/x-sql.md examples.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Consistent function naming across all documentation files.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: crawl.md uses lowercase: dom_first_text(), dom_base_uri(), load_and_select(@url, ...). x-sql.md uses uppercase: DOM_FIRST_TEXT(), DOM_BASE_URI(), DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT(@url, ...). Both forms appear to work (case-insensitive), but a first-time user reading one doc and copying to the other context would be confused.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The SQL engine accepts both uppercase and lowercase function names, but documentation was written by different authors at different times without a style guide.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Pick one convention (recommend uppercase DOM_* to match SQL convention) and standardize all documentation
- Add a note in both docs acknowledging the case-insensitivity
- Add a linter/CI check that validates all X-SQL examples in docs parse correctly
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: --format flag misleading without --sql — produces plain text, not structured output

sections.body: pwsh ./b4w.ps1 crawl --seed-file seeds.txt --depth 0 --format csv -o results.csv
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: CSV-formatted output with at least a URL column.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The output file contains human-readable plain text listing crawled pages, identical to the default (no --format) output. CSV/JSON formatting only activates when --sql is provided, since there are no columns to format.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The --format flag is a formatter for structured X-SQL result sets. Without --sql, there is no structured data, so the flag is silently ignored and the default plain-text page listing is emitted instead.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — crawl output formatting logic
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- When --format csv or --format json is specified without --sql, emit a default structured output with at least URL and title columns (from page metadata)
- Or emit a warning: '--format requires --sql to produce structured output; falling back to plain text'
- Document this dependency prominently in the --format flag description
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Stderr noise: 'Finding browser4 root from...' printed during crawl --sql operations

sections.body: pwsh ./b4w.ps1 crawl --seed-file seeds.txt --depth 0 --sql @query.sql --format json
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Clean output with only the crawl progress and results.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: A diagnostic line 'Finding browser4 root from /home/vincent/workspace/Browser4-4.12' appears on stderr before the crawl output, polluting both terminal display and JSON parsing.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ — SQL file resolution logic
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Move this message to a debug/trace log level, only shown with --verbose
- Or emit it to stderr only when the resolved path differs from the expected path
- Suppress all non-error stderr output when --json flag is active
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
